rv.q: Mischief Comedy’s latest theatrical assault on the funny bone is riotously entertaining, breathtakingly well executed and, quite simply, one of the funniest shows I have seen in a very long time.
Mischief have once again delivered a riotous night of comedy, chaos and theatrical mishaps.
If you’re looking for a brilliant night out and a show that delivers plenty of laughs, The Comedy About Spies is an easy recommendation.
Mischief fans and newbies alike will find plenty to enjoy here and will undoubtably refer to this as one of the company's greatest shows to date.
It genuinely is one of the most amusing shows to infiltrate the West End in years.
With its sharpened script, superb cast and relentless silliness, The Comedy About Spies proves this is a spy mission well worth revisiting.
If you're a fan of their work then this is them at the top of their game and if it has never particularly tickled your pickle, this may just be the one to change your mind.
This gloriously British romp will have you laughing so hard you’ll blow your cover.
If you are looking for pure, unadulterated escapism, The Comedy About Spies certainly delivers on laughs.
The second act is where the pace begins to drift.

cn.t: Mischief Theatre delivers another riotously funny hit with this 1960s spy spoof, earning near-universal praise for its relentless laughs, expertly timed slapstick, and gleefully ridiculous commitment to Cold War-era chaos.

vr.q: It is a five-star show. I loved it back in 2025 and 2026 is no exception.
